rules.rule: Select the most specific concept that is FULLY entailed by the span and its immediate context. Do not infer detail not present in the text. If a child concept adds detail not supported by the span, prefer the parent.
When a negative finding has a dedicated SNOMED concept, prefer the negative/absent form. When no negative form exists, annotate the positive concept — negation does not prevent annotation.
When candidates span multiple SNOMED hierarchies, use context to pick the right one. Default tie-break order: Procedure > Finding > Body structure.
Only consider context from the previous, current, and next sentence when disambiguating. Do not use distant parts of the note to over-specify a concept.

For physical objects (devices, catheters, implants), prefer the 'in situ' finding if the context describes presence, or the procedure if the context describes insertion/removal. Physical object hierarchy is out of scope.
Structured section headings are not annotations and should be ignored.
Expand abbreviations to their canonical meaning in the given section context before generating search terms. The section header is the strongest disambiguation signal for overloaded abbreviations.
When uncertain between a parent and child concept after applying all other rules, prefer the parent (broader) concept.
